rationale: Sharpens the event-backpressure account with two pieces of retained/source information that bear on severity and on the drain obligation: the retained run's own duration (all four cases, including the default-capacity case, finished in 21.69s of test time) and the documentation contrast between the event path and the decided-subscriber path.

interpretations.rationale: Current account. Source-settled mechanism: the actor publishes every observed transition with `event_tx.send(..).await` inside `detect_and_emit_events` (actor.rs:169-199), awaited from the tick arm of the single `run` select loop (actor.rs:665-711), on the channel spawn_actor builds as `async_channel::bounded(RuntimeConfig::event_capacity)` (handle.rs:295-323; knob handle.rs:34-35, default 1024 handle.rs:74). The handle owns a receiver from construction, so an application that never consumes the event stream still leaves it unread, and subscribe_events only hands out clones (handle.rs:254-259). A send that cannot fit parks the actor task, which then cannot run op.tick() (election heartbeats, resends, batch flushes), cannot handle incoming messages and cannot answer any Command - including the append_notify Timeout that drain_notifiers would have produced on that same tick path (actor.rs:201-222; endpoint at handle.rs:114-137). Retained support, execution bbff5b4cad8f47129ee5997bb6eee815 (experiment 90492867f1794b14afa6537c6a7b7951-experiment, exit 0, four cases passed, parsing_error_count 0): event 0 `default_capacity_parked_cluster` {event_capacity: 1024, nodes_parked: 2, decided_before: 1129, decided_after: 1129, append_notify_timeout_reached: true} shows the bound reached at the shipped default capacity and the healthy third node unable to move the decided index across a write that ended in the documented Timeout; event 3 `parked_majority_cluster` {nodes_parked: 2, healthy_node_responsive: true, decided_before: 3, decided_after: 3} repeats the cluster-level stall at capacity 8; events 4,5,6 (`unconsumed_event_bound_reached` {nodes_full: 2, nodes: 3}, `actor_parked` {node: 1, samples_without_reply: 10, permanently_parked: true}, `append_notify_endpoint_withheld` {node: 1, per_call_deadline_ms: 300, actor_timeout_ms: 1500, resolved: false}) give the node-local freeze; events 2,1 are the control with every stream drained (`control_actors_responsive` {nodes_answering: 3}, `control_append_notify` {origin: 1, succeeded: true, idx: 2}). Timescale, from the retained execution's own record: the four cases - including the default-capacity case that reaches 1129 decided entries before two nodes park - finished in 21.69s of test time (check.json started 06:54:37, ended 06:55:05 UTC) under ordinary paced client traffic (one write per millisecond from one origin, error-free in-process delivery, no message loss), i.e. at the shipped default an unconsumed event stream parks nodes and stops progress within seconds-to-tens-of-seconds of normal operation rather than after an implausible amount of work; that figure is a bound from one schedule, not a rate claim. Drain obligation, from the snapshot's own documentation: nothing in it requires the application to read the event stream - RuntimeConfig::event_capacity is described only as 'Bounded capacity for the event channel' (handle.rs:34-35), subscribe_events only offers clones and suggests wrapping in a broadcasting task for fan-out (handle.rs:254-259), and the handle holds a receiver from spawn_actor whether or not the application ever subscribes (handle.rs:295-323) - whereas the decided-subscriber path states the opposite policy explicitly ('slow subscribers apply backpressure by causing the actor to defer pushes rather than blocking the actor loop'). The comparison therefore holds: an unconsumed bounded event stream parks the actor loop at every measured capacity (8, 64, 1024) and the parked node loses every command endpoint including the documented failure; once enough nodes park the cluster stops deciding; with the same capacities and activity and a draining consumer nothing freezes. Counter-limitations kept in force: (a) the trigger is client-side - the defect rests on the handle-method contract and on the documented contrast with the decided-subscriber path, not on a documented promise about events; (b) a dropped receiver unblocks the actor, so the stall lasts exactly as long as a live unread receiver is held; (c) how many nodes a schedule parks is not bounded (case 1 witnesses at least one permanently parked node with two of three channels full; the cluster cases witness two of three); (d) the earlier harness revision's transport jam (run 8f27d10f, one node parked, spurious stall) is retained as an excluded cause, and the retained receipt uses the corrected per-destination delivery; (e) the 21.69s figure covers the whole four-case suite in one in-process schedule on one machine, so it bounds rather than measures a deployment's time to park.
limitations: The trigger is client-side and the snapshot documents no drain obligation for events; the finding rests on the Command/append_notify contract plus the documented deferral policy of the decided-subscriber path.
A dropped receiver unblocks the actor, so the stall is bounded by how long a live, unread receiver is held.
How many nodes a given schedule parks is not bounded: case 1 witnesses at least one permanently parked node (two of three channels full), the cluster cases witness two of three nodes parked.
The 21.69s suite duration bounds (does not measure) the time to park at the default capacity: one in-process schedule, one origin pacing writes at 1ms, error-free delivery.

The superseded harness revision's transport jam is retained as an excluded cause: run 8f27d10febbd45dbb6b854e8a2af08c6 stalled with only one node parked, and the retained receipt uses the corrected per-destination delivery.
